title: Derived quasi-coherent tests of pullback and inverse limits
statement: Use algebraic spaces over a scheme $S$ and their small etale sites and structure sheaves [def-trf-algebraic-space, def-pc-scheme], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Module sheaves and quasi-coherence are [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. Write $D(\mathcal O_Z)$ for the derived category of module sheaves [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] and $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Z)$ for its full subcategory of complexes with quasi-coherent cohomology sheaves. Sheaf tensor products are [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $f:Z\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ a flat proper finitely presented algebraic space. Spectra are [def-weil-affine-spectrum]; flatness and local finite presentation are tested on etale scheme charts [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Finite presentation means quasi-compact, quasi-separated and locally of finite presentation; quasi-separated means that the diagonal is quasi-compact. Proper means separated, quasi-compact, locally of finite type on etale charts, and universally closed; separated means the diagonal is a closed immersion and universally closed means closed after every algebraic-space base change [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $(M_n)_{n\ge1}$ be an inverse sequence of $A$-modules with surjective transition maps and set $M=\varprojlim_n M_n$, $\mathcal F=\mathcal O_Z\otimes_A M$, and $\mathcal G=\varprojlim_n(\mathcal O_Z\otimes_A M_n)$. The canonical map $u:\mathcal F\to\mathcal G$ induces a bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal O_Z)}(K,\mathcal F[0])\to\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal O_Z)}(K,\mathcal G[0])$ for every $K\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Z)$.

source.place: Tag 0D3F (lemma-pullback-and-limits); the first paragraph of its proof states precisely the universal derived-Hom formulation used here.

proof.text: Put $F_n=\mathcal O_Z\otimes_A M_n$. Apply the flat affine-base projection lemma to $f$ (properness gives quasi-compactness and separatedness, hence quasi-separatedness): every $F_n$ is quasi-coherent and the transitions are surjective. The surjective quasi-coherent tower lemma therefore identifies $\mathcal G[0]$ with $R\varprojlim_nF_n[0]$. All limits here are in the ambient module derived category; we do not assert that $\mathcal G$ is quasi-coherent.

Fix a perfect $E\in D(\mathcal O_Z)$ and put $E^\vee=R\mathcal Hom(E,\mathcal O_Z)$. Ringed-site perfect duality makes $E^\vee$ perfect and identifies $R\mathcal Hom(E,N)$ naturally with $E^\vee\otimes^{\mathbf L}N$ for every ambient $N$. Put $C=R\Gamma(Z,E^\vee)$. The flat proper perfect-sections lemma makes $C$ a perfect complex of $A$-modules. Applying the affine-base projection formula gives natural isomorphisms $R\operatorname{Hom}_Z(E,F_n[0])\cong C\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}M_n[0]$ and $R\operatorname{Hom}_Z(E,\mathcal F[0])\cong C\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}M[0]$. The projection formula applies to $E^\vee$, whose cohomology is quasi-coherent by the perfect-generation statement, which places every perfect object in that subcategory.

Apply global derived Hom to the identification of step 1, then use its derived-limit comparison and the natural isomorphisms of step 2. This identifies $R\operatorname{Hom}_Z(E,\mathcal G[0])$ with $R\varprojlim_n(C\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}M_n[0])$. Under these identifications $R\operatorname{Hom}_Z(E,u)$ is the canonical comparison $C\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}M[0]\to R\varprojlim_n(C\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}M_n[0])$: the cone is induced by the maps $M\to M_n$, and both the duality/projection isomorphisms and the resolution-derived comparison are natural for those maps. The perfect tensor-limit lemma says this comparison is an isomorphism. Taking $H^0$, using the cohomology identification in the global derived-Hom lemma, proves the required Hom bijection for every perfect $E$. This uses global Hom on the ambient derived category, so it remains valid for the possibly non-quasi-coherent limit.

Use Hom exactness for distinguished triangles (and its rotations and opposite-category form). Choose a distinguished triangle $\mathcal F[0]\xrightarrow{u}\mathcal G[0]\to Q\to\mathcal F[1]$. For every perfect $E$ and integer $r$, the previous step also applies to the perfect complex $E[-r]$; the long exact Hom sequence gives $\operatorname{Hom}(E,Q[r])=0$. Let $\mathcal L$ be the class of $K\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Z)$ with $\operatorname{Hom}(K,Q[r])=0$ for all integers $r$. The long exact Hom sequence makes $\mathcal L$ closed under shifts and cones; a retract of a zero Hom group is zero; and $\operatorname{Hom}(\bigoplus_iK_i,Q[r])=\prod_i\operatorname{Hom}(K_i,Q[r])$ by the coproduct universal property. Thus it is closed under retracts and all set-indexed coproducts and contains every perfect object. The algebraic-space localizing-generation theorem gives $\mathcal L=D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Z)$. For any such $K$, the segment $\operatorname{Hom}(K,Q[-1])\to\operatorname{Hom}(K,\mathcal F[0])\to\operatorname{Hom}(K,\mathcal G[0])\to\operatorname{Hom}(K,Q)$ has zero outside terms, which proves the asserted bijection.
